---
title: "Control"
---

Most Outlets and Pumps in the regional models are controlled by a DiscreteControl node.
Each has one of these functions, which decides when it lets water through, and the code that adds them is in `ribasim_nl.control`:

- `drain`: outlet draining an area
- `supply`: inlet supplying an area
- `flow_control`: flow through an area in supply (drought) and drain conditions
- `flushing`: an outlet with a specific flow to be maintained at any conditions (supply or drain)

This is what they do in terms of upstream and downstream levels, in the supply (aanvoer) or drain (afvoer) state:

| Function | Dutch | State determined by | Flow in supply state [m³/s] | Flow in drain state [m³/s] | Nodes added |
|:---------|:------|:--------------------|:---------------------|:--------------------|:------------|
| `drain` | uitlaat | upstream level | 0 | capacity | DiscreteControl |
| `supply` | inlaat | downstream level | capacity | 0 | DiscreteControl |
| `flow_control` | doorlaat | upstream and downstream level | capacity | capacity | DiscreteControl |
| `flushing` | doorspoeling | upstream level and flow rate | demand | capacity | DiscreteControl and FlowDemand |

Each controlled node gets two rows in its static table, for the control states `aanvoer` (supply) and `afvoer` (drain), and one DiscreteControl node with a control link.
The capacity in the table is `max_flow_rate`: a node lets through its `flow_rate`, limited by `max_flow_rate`.
Flushing nodes also get a FlowDemand node, which sets the flow to maintain, seasonal if it differs between summer and winter; their `flow_rate` in the supply state is 0.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "A drain node between two Basins. The DiscreteControl node listens to the level upstream and switches the state of the Outlet."
flowchart LR
  up["Basin upstream"] -->|flow| outlet["Outlet<br>afvoer: capacity<br>aanvoer: 0"]
  outlet -->|flow| down["Basin downstream"]
  dc["DiscreteControl"] -.->|control| outlet
  up -.->|listens to level| dc
```

## Levels and thresholds

The target level of a Basin is its `meta_streefpeil` in `Basin / area`.
From it follow the thresholds of the DiscreteControl nodes and the level limits of the nodes:

- The thresholds have a band of 5 cm in total around the level (`DEFAULT_LEVEL_THRESHOLD_RANGE`), so a node does not keep switching.
- `min_upstream_level` is the target level upstream, and in the supply state 4 cm below it, except for drain nodes, which keep the target level in both states.
- `max_downstream_level` in the supply state is the target level downstream.
- In the drain state, Pumps stop pumping into a Basin 20 cm above its target level (`MAALSTOP_LEVEL_OFFSET`). Outlets are limited by gravity, so they have no such limit.

The [summer and winter levels](seasonal-levels.qmd) later split each state into a winter and a summer variant, such as `afvoer zomer`.

## How nodes get their function

The two kinds of models get their function differently.

- **Gravity controlled**: `04_add_full_control.py` calls `add_controllers_to_supply_area` for each supply area, `verwerkt/sturing/aanvoergebieden.gpkg`. The inlets and outlets of the polygon, and lists by hand, give the function: inlets supply and outlets drain, the reverse of a supply or flow control node drains, downstream of supply nodes it is `flow_control`, and the rest drains, except the reverse of a drain node, which supplies. Then `add_controllers_to_uncontrolled_connector_nodes` handles the remaining Outlets and Pumps, without those in `exclude_nodes`. The priority is flushing, flow control, drain, supply; the rest again drains, except the reverse of a drain node.
- **Level controlled**: the `meta_categorie` of a node maps to a function, with exceptions in `set_node_functions`. This gives no flushing nodes.

## Exceptions

Some systems need more than a DiscreteControl node per connector:

- Noorderzijlvest and Wetterskip Fryslân use `set_continuous_level_control` in places.
- Rijnland uses `set_discrete_level_control`, with control states `stap n`.
- Aa en Maas, Limburg and Rijnland also add FlowDemand nodes in their own scripts. In Rijnland, Katwijk flushes at least 1.07 m³/s this way.
- The main water system has its own control with DiscreteControl, ContinuousControl and FlowDemand nodes, see [Main water system](main-watersystem.qmd#control-and-demands).

## Capacities

The capacity of a node is its `max_flow_rate`.
In the gravity controlled models it comes from the reviewed `static_data.xlsx`, with `flow_rate_mm_per_day` as the default by node type and function, and `flow_rate` is often higher, so `max_flow_rate` decides.
The level controlled models set the unknown capacities from the area they drain or supply, and their `flow_rate` to the same value, see [design capacities](design-capacities.qmd).
